A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UserLM study. Their complete text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original model-training evaluations, behavioral and robustness experiments, and coding/math conversation simulations, with additional analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports a train–test overlap diagnostic in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The intent-conditioned dialogue-flipping procedure, Llama-based models, and conversation-termination token are unchanged. The generation guardrails highlighted in v2 Section 4.1 already appear in v1 Appendix C.1.

E1.justification: Both use WildChat, PRISM, CommonsenseQA, NaturalQuestions, and GSM8K/HumanEval-derived simulation tasks. The new overlap diagnostic examines existing WildChat splits without expanding dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same Llama baselines, USP-8b, and GPT-4o/4o-mini where applicable. V2 discloses a prompt-selection criterion, but the final role-playing prompts in Figure 9 are unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix A adds a diagnostic procedure measuring train–test 7-gram overlap among first-turn user prompts. Existing splits, training budgets, simulator-evaluation metrics, and simulation settings remain unchanged; the prompt-selection statement is newly disclosed documentation.

E4.justification: V2 adds a limited analysis checking the effectiveness of deduplication and user-based splitting in Appendix A. Existing intent-conditioning and checkpoint ablations, per-turn analyses, and simulation case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both report ten simulations per task intent with the same aggregation procedures. No seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are added or removed; conversational turn variance remains a behavioral metric.

E6.justification: Appendix A newly reports 4.19% train–test 7-gram overlap. Existing results in Tables 1–5 and the figures are unchanged, including Table 3's GPT-4o assistant scores of 74.6 with the GPT-4o simulator and 57.4 with UserLM-8b.

T1.justification: The perplexity formula and simulation-metric definitions in Appendix C.3 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, theorems, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about intent-conditioned UserLMs, simulation fidelity and robustness, and more challenging assistant evaluations. The headline 74.6% to 57.4% result is unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new overlap result as evidence that filtering and splitting minimize leakage. Section 5 removes the discussion advocating more open-source base models, while retaining cautions about personalization, specific populations, and expert domains.

D1.justification: Section 2.2 newly states that baseline prompt variants were selected using WildChat validation perplexity. Appendix D retains the same prompts without adding the promised selection details. Training hyperparameters, hardware, guardrail implementation, and model-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list and substantive positioning relative to prompted and fine-tuned user simulators are unchanged. Section 6 is shortened without adding or removing cited works or redefining the contribution.

P1.justification: Localized edits tighten experimental descriptions, discussion, and related work, clarify metric explanations, and standardize terminology. A discussion paragraph is removed and a funding acknowledgment added, while the overall section and appendix structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Conference headers replace preprint headers, and text wrapping and pagination change, including spacing around Table 3. All ten figures and five tables retain their contents and designs.

improvement.justification: V2 adds limited evidence supporting split integrity through Appendix A's overlap check, discloses the baseline prompt-selection criterion, and makes existing simulation guardrails more visible. These improve transparency and presentation modestly. The reproducibility gain remains incomplete because Appendix D does not supply the promised prompt-selection details.
